reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 4 recyclers trading the same material (78% of its feedstock)
Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 343% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
Sold products equal only 16% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
Electricity bought is only 0.40x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (121 kWh/t against at least 300)
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 25% of months
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.30x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
